setter.evidence: Almost certainly a direct, unset booking. The prospect found Trevor the previous night — 'he was the first guy that I clicked on last night that had a link to training and not just a PDF to download' — and the internal CRM walkthrough the same day confirms that bookings without initials in the title are not sets.

prospect.name: Sam
prospect.location: Western North Carolina, USA; on the call from Georgia for the July 4th weekend. Previously lived out of Airbnbs, largely in Colorado. Moving house before the baby arrives.
prospect.occupation: Healthcare startup, works remotely, in a sales role — 'I'm in sales. Nothing's ever a 10' and 'I've been in sales roles too.' Sits or stands at a desk with some walking calls.
prospect.family_status: Married three years. Wife is pregnant with their first child, a girl, due 2 November; he describes it as 'a complicated pregnancy to say the least', with appointments most Mondays near his in-laws so they travel most weekends. Planning to move before the birth.
prospect.training_background: Serious endurance athlete. Several 100-mile races, multiple marathons, road cycling 50 to 100 miles a week across three or four days, backcountry skiing, mountaineering — climbed and skied Mount Hood and Mount Adams in early June. Was a competitive cyclist growing up. Currently trains eight to ten hours a week: three bike days, three run days and four strength sessions, with strength deliberately kept to 20 minutes or less using a bench, dumbbells and a pull-up bar behind his desk. Bought kettlebells about two months ago and does roughly four kettlebell sessions a week chosen at random from social media. Upcoming objectives: climb and ski the highest mountain in California next June, and swim 12 miles across Lake Tahoe in August. Tracks food in Cronometer and has had a DEXA scan.
prospect.medical: Has dislocated both shoulders, on multiple occasions and by multiple mechanisms — 'Mountain biking, fly fishing, rolling over in bed, driving a dirt bike into a garage.' He self-restricts as a result: 'I can do some light snatches with a kettlebell, I can do presses, things like that. I would never, ever do a overhead barbell. I'll or ever go like full extension on pull-ups. I'll do pull-ups, but they'll always be a slight bit of' bend. No other conditions disclosed. Chronically under-slept by choice — 'I know sleep is important. I know I should prioritize it more, but I just give less of a about my sleep.'

signals: Self-directed and demonstrably capable — 100-mile races, volcano ascents, DEXA scans, macro tracking — and states plainly that he will succeed without help: 'I know that like, one way or another, like, I'll get to where I want to be'

Anchored hard to a cheap alternative he intends to compare against: 'going to that Future app and comparing, just like, you know, what's $199?' and a stated ceiling of '$250 a month was the maximum that I was ready to pull the trigger on'
Explicitly price-shopping on arrival — 'I was just going to go with the first, uh, option that was within my price range' — having found Trevor the previous night

Frames the decision as a time-versus-money trade rather than a capability gap: 'if it took me on my own eight months or nine months, would I get to the same point, but just be slower at it? And with less of a financial investment'

Overlap with the_optimizer is real — already fit, no rescue needed, wants good to great — but the defining feature of this call is a hard budget ceiling and an active cheaper substitute, which is the bargain-hunter shape
Unusual wrinkle: he works in sales himself, evaluated the process out loud — 'the order that you've been going through it from a sales perspective, I'm impressed' — and offered the rep a job

It's like, just wondering, you know, if it, if it took me on my own eight months or nine months, uh, would I get to the same point, but just be slower at it? And with less of a financial investment, that's kind of where my head's at.
objections.rep_response: Argued expertise and speed — 'he is kind of the number one person on the planet for kettlebells' and 'I don't think you'd probably get it to a level where he could get you even' — then, when that did not land, moved to price. Never asked why the prospect had not already done it on his own, which the rep identified as the core miss in his own debrief the same day.

objections.raw_quote: Got it. Got it. Higher than anticipated. Uh, I was thinking like 250 a month was the maximum that I was ready to pull the trigger on right now.
objections.rep_response: Isolated value from money correctly — 'outside of finances though, do you feel that everything we covered will solve all the things that we're looking for?' — and diagnosed it as a value question rather than an affordability one. Then, instead of running the financial picture or building value, dropped the price twice: to $3,000 for three months and then to $1,200 for one month, and finally added a seven-day refund.

objections.raw_quote: Are there any other, uh, Any other paths to work within your program? like, you know, the minute that I saw, and I think part of the reason why I went through this path was, or got on this call today, was like, I saw where it wasn't necessarily him on the phone I'd be talking to. Like, are there other trainers or anything that don't command such a high price point? Are there other people on his team?
objections.rep_response: Told him no such option exists: 'No, all the stuff, all the stuff we do is one-on-one with Trevor, so we don't have it, we don't have anybody else's.' Primal University exists at roughly $2,000 annually and the rep acknowledged the next day that this prospect was a candidate for it.

objections.raw_quote: So I think the answer is I got to go back and think more about it. I'm not going make a decision on this call to spend five times the amount that I was originally thinking of, but I appreciate your respect, why you guys do it like that. And I'm thankful for your willingness to get creative on the pricing.
objections.rep_response: Asked the right isolating question — 'what's coming up for us to sort through on that? Like what are we actually weighing on that?' — which produced the real answer, that he would go price-compare on Instagram. Then made at least five further attempts to close after this refusal, including invoking the unborn baby, before accepting a text follow-up.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: A seven-day full refund, invented on this call and warranted twice: 'If you don't like it in seven days, we'll refund it. If you're in your, like, I don't like it, we'll just refund it' and 'I'll, we'll put it in writing. If you don't like it, we'll just... Refund you within seven days' and 'it's on a recorded call here. We'll send you the call or refund it within seven days if you don't like it.' The manager confirmed the following session that no such policy exists. The standard performance guarantee was never mentioned.

prospect_financials.note: None obtained. No financial-picture question was asked at any point. The only figure on the table is his self-declared ceiling: 'the max I would be willing to spend was like two 50 a month.'

evidence: No payment and an explicit refusal to pay: 'Let me think about it. I'm not going to swipe a card on this call for that much, but I appreciate it.'
No payment link sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply.
He declined a decision outright: 'I'm not going make a decision on this call to spend five times the amount that I was originally thinking of.'
Next step owned by the rep and informal: 'I'll send you a text in a couple of days. Just let me know what you're thinking.'

Counter-evidence, positive: he rated the fit a seven or eight, said 'if the price makes sense, you know, sign up today', called it 'a good call and very informational', praised the model — 'Love the university kind of model mindset' — and volunteered that he would tell the rep if it were a firm no.

Counter-evidence, negative and decisive: his stated intent on leaving was to go price-shop. 'I will probably just get on Instagram and just like, find some price comparisons', against a named alternative at $199 a month.
The rep's own read the same day was that this was close — 'I was so close to getting him across the line' — and the manager's read was that there was never enough of a value gap for the price.
outcome.next_step: Rep to text in a couple of days. In his manager 1-1 immediately afterwards the rep proposed phoning the prospect and downselling him to Primal University — the cheaper product he had told the prospect on this call did not exist.

notable.note: The most serious call in the batch on both axes. Clinically, a prospect who has dislocated both shoulders repeatedly, including by rolling over in bed, was told that shoulder injuries are 'just completely gone' after the programme and moved toward snatches and pressing, with no clinician clearance raised. Commercially, the price fell from $6,000 to $3,000 to $1,200 inside about twenty minutes on hesitation alone, with no financial-picture question asked at any point; the $3,000 three-month figure is $1,000 below the company's actual three-month price; and a seven-day full refund was invented, promised 'in writing' and expressly warranted on the recorded call, when no refund policy exists. Separately, the prospect asked directly whether a lower-priced option existed and was told no, while Primal University at roughly $2,000 a year does exist — the rep proposed selling him exactly that the next day. The pressure at the end is also notable: at least five re-closes after a clear refusal, including 'your baby girl's coming in four months, bro... it's taken away directly from time with your girl' and then 'You're a silly goose, bro. You're a silly goose, Sam.' Worth recording that the discovery on this call was genuinely strong and that the prospect, himself a salesperson, complimented it and offered the rep a job.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion throughout, with the prospect labelled only 'sam'. Whole rep passages sit under the prospect's label — the entire injury-resolution claim at 00:36:02, the $1,200 offer at 00:52:58 and the closing pressure sequence at 01:00:21 onward are all mislabelled, and several turns fuse both speakers with no break. The final third is the worst affected, which matters because that is where the pricing and refund statements occur; every quote used in the flags file was attributed by content and cross-checked against the rep's own account of this call in his manager 1-1 the same day.
